alignments.note: Participle predicated of the written subject.
Object marker with no English of its own (rule 16).
Noun with the supplied *the*, which determines the nominal expression and is not added (rule 15).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun, headed on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
Conjunction rendered by the adversative *But*, which rule 14's open list covers.
Construct noun with a supplied *the*; no article morpheme stands in the chain (rule 29). The ASV writes a noun for it, so rule 19's `דֶּרֶךְ` → *toward* case does not arise.
Nomen rectum with the chain's *of* (rule 19) and the supplied *the* its anarthrous substantival adjective licenses (rule 46), headed on the word carrying the lexeme.

Finite verb with its subject pronoun and the phrasal particle completing the rendering; *turn* alone does not write the making-crooked, so the particle stays with the verb (rule 44). The marginal 'Or, maketh crooked' was read and set aside (rule 38).

review_notes: The waw opening the last colon takes the adversative *But* written for it (rule 14).
The marginal alternative 'Or, maketh crooked' was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
